meta.description: Register of official sources used in this project. Every verified value in this project traces to a source on this register. 'fetch_method' records exactly how the value was obtained: 'direct-fetch' (page downloaded and read) or 'search-snapshot' (search-engine snippet of the official page; treated as UNVERIFIED until direct fetch).

sources.name: World Gold Council — Gold spot prices (Goldhub)
sources.used_for: Primary gold spot price anchor: USD 4,024.36/oz, data as of 21 October 2026.
sources.notes: Page states: 'Market Data: Provided by ICE Data Services' and 'Data as of 21 October, 2026'.

sources.name: LBMA — Precious Metal Prices (benchmark administered by ICE Benchmark Administration)
sources.used_for: Reference for what the LBMA Gold Price is (twice-daily auction administered by IBA). Numeric values now licence-gated via MyLBMA/ICE; NOT used for any number in this project.
sources.notes: IRREGULARITY FLAG: numeric LBMA price data requires an IBA licence since 18 Mar 2025 per World Gold Council page; public sites may lag or differ.

sources.name: eCFR — 16 CFR Part 23, FTC Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries
sources.used_for: Gold-content marking rules (§23.3), quality-mark and maker's-mark rules (§23.10), weight representation (§23.18). Content 'up to date as of 10/21/2026'.
sources.notes: §23.3(c)(1) expressly allows karat designations such as '9 Karat Gold' when correctly disclosed — the 10K threshold was removed from the 2018 revision.

sources.name: U.S. Code (govinfo) — 15 U.S.C. ch. 8 §§291–296, National Gold and Silver Stamping Act of 1906 (as amended 1976)
sources.used_for: Fineness tolerance: whole-article assay (incl. solder) may not be below the marked fineness by more than 3/1000 (watchcases, flatware) or 7/1000 (all other articles) — §295. §294 prohibits falsely marked gold ware in commerce.
sources.notes: 1976 amendment (Pub. L. 94–450) replaced the old 'one-half of one carat' / 'one carat' tolerances with the 3/1000 and 7/1000 standards.

sources.name: 15 U.S.C. §297 (trademark/maker's mark requirement), as cited in eCFR §23.10
sources.used_for: Requirement that a quality mark be accompanied by the trademark or name of the manufacturer/dealer (National Stamping Act), quoted inside eCFR §23.10 'Disclosure of identity of manufacturers, processors, or distributors'.

sources.name: FTC — Statement of Basis and Purpose, Final Revisions to the Jewelry Guides (Aug 2018)
sources.used_for: Background on 2018 Jewelry Guide revisions (plating thickness definitions, karat disclosure).

sources.name: The Goldsmiths' Company Assay Office (London) — Hallmarking
sources.used_for: Independent assay/hallmarking reference; hallmarking since 1300; UK fineness options incl. 9, 14, 18, 22 carat, 990, 999 gold (per their calculator).
